Cobordism experiment — synthesis & realizability: results¶

What the synthesis & realizability layer (§4b boundary synthesis + §5.0 realizability) built, and what it shows. Companion to the runnable capstone examples/cobordism/realizability_report.py and to the experiment charter cobordism.md §4b, §5.0; mirrors the Stage-1/Stage-2 reports (cobordism-stage2-report.md).

Verdict¶

The realizability hypothesis is supported. Bending an operation \(U\) to its Choi state and synthesizing the bulk spectrally (pin the boundary, fill the interior, drive the §4b residual to zero) cleanly separates the two outcomes the hypothesis predicts: a realizable \(U\) is realized with its bulk \(W_{AB}\) (\(r\to 0\)), and an obstructed \(U\) is certified non-realizable by a residual floor bounded away from zero — a spectral obstruction under the fixed-boundary constraint, not a failure to search hard enough. The capstone runs clean, deterministic, and exit 0:

State-Operation-Cobordism correspondence -- synthesis + realizability

       two-vertex seed floors at r = 3.602e-03  (general qubit is not a K_2 eigenvector)
       geo(ψ): converged=True  r=9.387e-10  complexity |V|=3 |E|=3  cones=1  λ=0.199908

The three formal correspondence claims hold too, on a realized witness: \(W_{AB}=\mathrm{geo}(U)\) is a cobordism, its boundary is \(\overline{\mathrm{geo}(\psi_B)}\sqcup\mathrm{geo}(\psi_A)\), and \(Z(W_{AB})=\langle\psi_A|U|\psi_B\rangle\) (in its spectral/Choi reading; bridging to the Dijkgraaf–Witten state-sum is the open follow-up) — see The three correspondence hypotheses below.

§5.0 reframed: realizability is spectral bulk synthesis¶

The sharp question is §5.0: given an operation \(U:\mathcal H_B\to\mathcal H_A\), find a bulk 3-manifold \(W_{AB}\) that realizes it, or prove none exists. The realizability test here is not TQFT-membership \(Z(W)=U\) generated by the modular \(S,T\) — that route is set aside. The Dijkgraaf–Witten state-sum of §5.3–5.5 remains the topological invariant tested by Stage-2’s T1–T5; realizability is decided spectrally: \(U\) is realizable iff a bulk can be synthesized whose boundary Laplacian carries the bent operator as an eigenvector.

The crucial point is that this is not the free coning of §4b. In §4b the parameters outrun the constraints and any single eigenvector is eventually realizable by growing the complex. In §5.0 the boundaries are pinned (the synthesized \(\mathrm{geo}(\psi_A)\), \(\mathrm{geo}(\psi_B)\) and the output surface), so this is an interior fill with fixed ends. A target is realizable iff the residual can be driven to zero, and unrealizable iff it floors away from zero: non-existence is certified by an obstruction (a residual floor), the analogue of §4b’s two-vertex floor, not by exhausting triangulations.

The three correspondence hypotheses¶

The state–operation–cobordism correspondence makes three formal claims about the bulk \(W_{AB}\) synthesized for an operation \(U\). The capstone evaluates each explicitly (verify_correspondence) on a realized witness (the zero-mode \(U=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{psmallmatrix}\)); all three hold.

  1. \(W_{AB} = \mathrm{geo}(U)\) is a cobordism. The bulk produced by bending \(U\) and filling the interior is a genuine manifold-with-boundary — a nonempty codim-1 boundary together with interior cells carrying the fill (\(4\) boundary edges, \(1\) interior edge on the witness). True by construction (the bulk is assembled from the boundary geo’s and an interior the fill writes) and checked structurally via Spacetime.getBoundary().

  2. \(\partial W_{AB} = \overline{\mathrm{geo}(\psi_B)}\ \sqcup\ \mathrm{geo}(\psi_A)\). The boundary is the (outgoing) \(\mathrm{geo}(\psi_A)\) and the orientation-reversed (incoming) \(\mathrm{geo}(\psi_B)\). getBoundary() on the witness returns exactly the pinned boundary edges and excludes the interior, and the fill leaves those boundary edges byte-identical (it only ever rewrites interior edges): on the bipyramid witness \(\partial W=\{(0,2),(0,3),(1,2),(1,3)\}\) with the interior edge \((0,1)\) excluded and pinned. The explicit two-ends-with-orientation decomposition is built by the gluing and shown panel-by-panel in the companion visualization (issue #166).

  3. \(Z(W_{AB}) = \langle\psi_A|\,U\,|\psi_B\rangle\). The cobordism’s value equals the transition amplitude. Two facts combine: (a) the realized \(W_{AB}\) carries \(\mathrm{vec}(U)\) as its output-boundary \(L\)-eigenvector (overlap \(=1.000000\)), so the cobordism’s boundary spectral data is the bent operator; and (b) the Stage-1 Hilbert–Schmidt / Choi identity \(\langle\psi_A|U|\psi_B\rangle = \langle\mathrm{vec}(U_T)\mid\mathrm{vec}(U)\rangle = \mathrm{Tr}(U_T^\dagger U)\) — with \(U_T=\lvert\psi_A\rangle\langle\psi_B\rvert\), computed by ChoiJamiolkowski.transitionAmplitude and verified equal to the direct \(\psi_A^\dagger U\psi_B\). Contracting the cobordism’s boundary state \(\mathrm{vec}(U)\) against the test functional \(\mathrm{vec}(U_T)\) for any \(\psi_A,\psi_B\) therefore returns \(\langle\psi_A|U|\psi_B\rangle\) — i.e. \(Z(W_{AB})\) read off the synthesized boundary reproduces the amplitude (run: \(Z = 1.2522 - 0.6261i = \langle\psi_A|U|\psi_B\rangle\)).

    Honest scope. This establishes \(Z(W_{AB})\) as the spectral / Choi reading of the cobordism value — the boundary state contracted with the test functional — not an independently-computed Dijkgraaf–Witten state-sum. The DW invariant is the topological-layer object (Stage 2, §5.3–5.5); bridging the spectral \(Z\) to the DW state-sum on the same \(W_{AB}\) is the open follow-up.

Method¶

The oracle (cobordism::RealizabilityOracle) is pure orchestration of the merged, separately-tested classes — ChoiJamiolkowski (the bend), EigenstateSynthesis (the fixed-boundary interior-fill engine), and the multi-restart LevenbergMarquardt least-squares solver the §4b GeometrySynthesizer already drives. The recipe per \(U\):

  1. Bend. \(U \mapsto \mathrm{vec}(U)\) via Choi–Jamiołkowski (the operator-as-state, row-major). This is the boundary state the bulk must carry.

  2. Pin \(\partial W\). Hold the bulk’s boundary edges fixed (the synthesized \(\mathrm{geo}\)’s / the output surface). The fill only ever rewrites interior edges, so \(\partial W\) is byte-identical before and after.

  3. Fill the interior. Solve for the interior Hermitian edge weights and — via the boundary-fixed Pachner add — the interior topology, so the output-boundary \(k=0\) graph-Laplacian eigenvector matches the bent target, minimizing the §4b eigenvalue-agnostic residual $\( r(W) = \big\lVert (I-\psi\psi^\dagger)\,L\,\psi \big\rVert^2,\qquad L=D-A,\ D_{ii}=\textstyle\sum_j|A_{ij}|. \)$

  4. Verdict. Realizable iff \(r\) is driven below \(\epsilon=10^{-10}\) (the witness \(W_{AB}\) is returned, \(L\psi\parallel\psi\)); obstructed iff \(r\) floors at a positive value — the floor is the non-existence certificate, cross-checked against an independent numpy global-min over the interior edge.

The three headline cases exercise the three regimes:

  • Minimal-complexity realization (zero mode). \(U=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{psmallmatrix}=2\lvert+\rangle\langle+\rvert\): \(\mathrm{vec}(U)\) is the constant vector, the exact zero mode of \(L=D-A\) for any phase-0 positive-weight boundary. Realized on the bipyramid at minimal interior complexity (interior_vertex_count = 0): the fill only has to keep the lone interior edge at phase 0, so \(\lambda=0\).

  • Realization after interior growth. A generic \(1\times3\) operation \(U=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&0.3+0.5i&-0.8+0.2i\end{psmallmatrix}\) on the solid triangle: not an eigenvector of the bare pinned triangle, so it floors at the seed, but the fixed-boundary cone-and-retry grows the interior (one cone) and realizes it — the §5.0 analogue of §4b coning, with the boundary pinned.

  • Certified obstruction. \(U=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{psmallmatrix}\), \(\mathrm{vec}(U)=(1,2,3,4)\): a generic state not realizable as a bipyramid-boundary eigenvector against the pinned boundary with a single interior edge. With no growth budget the residual floors at \(r=2.35\times10^{-2}\), bounded away from zero — certified non-realizable.

Results¶

| operation \(U\) | bulk | verdict | \(r\) / floor | cones | interior \(|V|\) | \(\lambda\) | |—|—|—|—|—|—|—| | \(\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{psmallmatrix}\) (zero mode) | bipyramid | realizable | \(r=9.49\times10^{-11}\) | 0 | 0 | \(0.000000\) | | \(\begin{psmallmatrix}1&0.3{+}0.5i&-0.8{+}0.2i\end{psmallmatrix}\) (\(1\times3\)) | triangle | realizable | \(r=1.19\times10^{-13}\) | 1 | 1 | \(3.923719\) | | \(\begin{psmallmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{psmallmatrix}\) (generic) | bipyramid | obstructed | floor \(=2.35\times10^{-2}\) | 0 | 0 | \(1.176471\) |

Boundary synthesis (§4b), the input to the above: the general-amplitude qubit \(\psi=(\sqrt{0.8},\sqrt{0.2})\), \(|c_0|\ne|c_1|\), floors at \(r=3.60\times10^{-3}\) on the two-vertex seed \(K_2\) (it is not a balanced two-vertex eigenvector) and is synthesized as \(\mathrm{geo}(\psi)\) on the minimal complex \(K_3\) — \(|V|=3\), \(|E|=3\), one cone, \(r=9.39\times10^{-10}\), \(\lambda=0.199908\).

The realizable residuals (\(\sim10^{-11}\) and \(\sim10^{-13}\)) sit nine to twelve orders of magnitude below the obstruction floor (\(2.35\times10^{-2}\)): the separation is unambiguous. The certified floor matches an independent numpy grid global-min over the single interior edge to \(\Delta=3.0\times10^{-4}\), so the floor is a genuine non-existence certificate, not a stuck optimizer.

Key findings¶

  1. The realizability boundary is sharp and an obstruction is generic at fixed complexity. Interpolating \(U(t)\) from the uniform zero mode to \(\begin{psmallmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{psmallmatrix}\) on the one-interior-edge bipyramid (no growth budget), the residual lifts off zero immediately (\(t=0\): \(9.5\times10^{-11}\), realizable; \(t=0.1\): \(5.3\times10^{-3}\), floored) and saturates near \(2.4\times10^{-2}\). Obstruction is therefore not a measure-zero accident — an open set of operations is unrealizable at fixed boundary and interior.

  2. The floor is a genuine certificate, not a stuck solver. It is seed-independent and reproduces an independent numpy global-min over the lone interior edge (\(2.352941\times10^{-2}\) certified vs \(2.382794\times10^{-2}\) on a coarse grid). The certified value \(2.35\times10^{-2}\) is exactly \(2/85\) (to machine precision) — a clean closed form, as in the §4b two-vertex floor.

  3. Growth converts an obstruction into a realization — obstruction is relative to complexity. The generic \(1\times3\) \(U\) floors at \(9.6\times10^{-1}\) with budget 0 but drops to \(1.2\times10^{-13}\) with a single boundary-fixed cone. The floor certifies non-realizability at the current boundary and interior; coning is the canonical simplicial way to add interior freedom, and interior_vertex_count == cones_applied throughout.

  4. The zero mode needs no growth. The constant vector is the exact zero mode of \(L=D-A\) for any phase-0 positive-weight boundary, so the uniform \(U\) is realized at interior_vertex_count = 0 with \(\lambda=0\) — the fill merely keeps the lone interior edge at phase 0. This is the minimal-complexity end of the realizable spectrum.

  5. §4b and §5.0 share one mechanism. Both decide membership by a residual that either reaches zero (realizable) or floors (obstructed), and both grow the complex by topology-preserving coning. §5.0 adds the one structural twist that makes realizability a test rather than a foregone conclusion: the boundary is pinned, so the interior fill has fixed ends.

Conventions¶

  • Operators are flat row-major; \(\mathrm{vec}(U)\) is the row-major flatten, equal to ChoiJamiolkowski.vectorize — the Choi bend.

  • The \(k=0\) Laplacian keeps the magnitude degree convention \(D_{ii}=\sum_j|A_{ij}|\) (Hermitian \(L\), unitary evolution); the eigenvalue is the Rayleigh quotient \(\lambda=\psi^\dagger L\psi\).

  • The boundary \(\partial W\) is pinned: the fill rewrites only interior edges, so \(\partial W\) is byte-identical before and after the synthesis.

  • Realizable iff \(r<\epsilon=10^{-10}\); the obstruction certificate is a floor bounded above \(10^{-2}\) (and there floor == residual).

  • Seeded and reproducible; the 10-CPU cap is honored (thread env set at launch).

Reproduce¶

poetry run pip install -e .
poetry run python examples/cobordism/realizability_report.py   # the table above
poetry run python -m pytest tests/cobordism/test_realizability_oracle_python.py
poetry run python -m pytest tests/cobordism/test_geometry_synthesizer_python.py

--seed (default 0), --restarts (default 80), and --no-plot are available; the §7 sweeps (the realizability boundary \(U(t)\) and the interior-fill cone-budget series) and the §8 figures are written to /tmp/cobordism/ and are not committed — the script is the committed artifact. Attach them to the issue/PR to pin a result.
